top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Updates target ABI argument classification for transparent_union parameters so extend/sign-extend ABIArgInfo records receive the already-converted LLVM coercion type. The change affects AArch64, ARM, X86-32, and RISC-V paths, with RISC-V's extendType extended to accept and propagate an optional CoerceTy.
Changed symbols: RISCVABIInfo::extendType; RISCVABIInfo::classifyArgumentType; AArch64ABIInfo::classifyArgumentType; ARMABIInfo::classifyArgumentType; X86_32ABIInfo::classifyArgumentType; ABIArgInfo::getExtend; ABIArgInfo::getExtendInReg; ABIArgInfo::getSignExtend
Behavioral change: ABI extension classifications now retain CGT.ConvertType(Ty) as their coercion type rather than relying only on the source QualType.; RISC-V extendType forwards the supplied coercion type to getSignExtend or getExtend.; The affected behavior is target calling-convention lowering for extendable transparent_union function parameters.
Pass or subsystem link: Clang target ABI code generation
Causal explanation: This commit is in Clang CodeGen, but the retrieved changes are confined to ABI argument-extension/coercion metadata for transparent_union parameters. They do not touch asm goto lowering, loop construction, ScalarEvolution, SCEVExpander, isKnownSentinel, or loop-exit-value rewriting. A connection would require the reproducer to involve one of these target-specific transparent_union calling-convention paths, which is not evidenced by the retrieved hunks.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: Changes a shared ABIArgInfo construction interface and updates multiple target implementations.; The retrieved hunks show no asm-goto or optimizer regression test coverage.

The SVE/SME loops deliberately use `Value *&` so assignments continue to update elements of `Ops`, preserving the prior indexed-loop mutation behavior.

Summary: This Clang C++ ABI/code-generation change consistently uses `CodeGenModule::GlobalsInt8PtrTy` instead of the general `Int8PtrTy` for vtables, VTTs, RTTI descriptors, virtual function pointer loads, and vtable components. top_candidates.subject: [clang][CodeGen] Fix GPU-specific attributes being dropped by bitcode linking
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This Clang CodeGen change prevents default function-definition attribute merging from overwriting target-feature attributes on functions imported from linked GPU bitcode. It adds a SetTargetFeatures control to GetCPUAndFeaturesAttributes, disables target-feature replacement in mergeDefaultFunctionDefinitionAttributes, and adds CUDA/AMDGPU bitcode-linking tests that verify preservation of +gfx11-insts attributes.

+// Verify the behavior of the +gfxN-insts in the way that
+// rocm-device-libs should be built with. e.g. If the device libraries has a function
+// with "+gfx11-insts", that attribute should still be present after linking and not
+// overwritten with the current target's settings.
+
+// This is important because at this time, many device-libs functions that are only
+// available on some GPUs put an attribute such as "+gfx11-insts" so that
+// AMDGPURemoveIncompatibleFunctions can detect & remove them if needed.
+
+// Build the fake device library in the way rocm-device-libs should be built.
+//
+// RUN: %clang_cc1 -x cl -triple amdgcn-amd-amdhsa\
+// RUN:   -mcode-object-version=none -emit-llvm-bc \
+// RUN:   %S/Inputs/ocml-sample-target-attrs.cl -o %t.bc
+
+// Check the default behavior
+// RUN: %clang_cc1 -x hip -triple amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -target-cpu gfx803 -fcuda-is-device \
+// RUN:   -mlink-builtin-bitcode %t.bc \
+// RUN:   -emit-llvm %s -o - | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=CHECK,INTERNALIZE
+
+// RUN: %clang_cc1 -x hip -triple amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -target-cpu gfx1101 -fcuda-is-device \
+// RUN:   -mlink-builtin-bitcode %t.bc -emit-llvm %s -o - | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=CHECK,INTERNALIZE
+
+// Check the case where no internalization is performed
+// RUN: %clang_cc1 -x hip -triple amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -target-cpu gfx803 \
+// RUN:   -fcuda-is-device -mlink-bitcode-file %t.bc -emit-llvm %s -o -  | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=CHECK,NOINTERNALIZE
+
+// Check the case where no internalization is performed
+// RUN: %clang_cc1 -x hip -triple amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -target-cpu gfx1101 \
+// RUN:   -fcuda-is-device -mlink-bitcode-file %t.bc -emit-llvm %s -o - | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=CHECK,NOINTERNALIZE
+
+
+// CHECK: define {{.*}} i64 @do_intrin_stuff() #[[ATTR:[0-9]+]]
+// INTERNALIZE: attributes #[[ATTR]] = {{.*}} "target-cpu"="gfx{{.*}}" "target-features"="+gfx11-insts"
+// NOINTERNALIZE: attributes #[[ATTR]] = {{.*}} "target-features"="+gfx11-insts"
+
+#define __device__ __attribute__((device))
+#define __global__ __attribute__((global))
+
+typedef unsigned long ulong;
+
+extern "C" {
+__device__ ulong do_intrin_stuff(void);
+
+__global__ void kernel_f16(ulong* out) {
+    *out = do_intrin_stuff();
+  }
+}

The retrieved TargetInfo.cpp removals and new ARM/ARC files are consistent with relocation rather than a visible change to asm-goto, loop, or optimizer semantics.

Pass or subsystem link: Clang OpenCL/SPIR-V CodeGen

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change corrects C++ constructor/destructor this-argument typing, especially for Microsoft ABI virtual destructor variants. It changes the ABI query from accepting a CXXMethodDecl to accepting a GlobalDecl, allowing the destructor variant to select the appropriate complete-object or deleting-destructor this type when arranging function signatures and emitting member calls.

Behavioral change: getThisArgumentTypeForMethod now receives a GlobalDecl and can distinguish constructor/destructor variants rather than only the underlying method declaration.; For Microsoft ABI virtual destructors, complete destructors use the parent record directly, while other variants use deleting-destructor lookup to obtain the shared this-adjustment behavior.; C++ structor declaration arrangement and call emission now pass variant-bearing GlobalDecl values, including explicit complete-constructor selection for one member-call path.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This CodeGen change propagates an explicit known-non-null property through Address construction and pointer replacement. Stack allocas, return-value storage, and a constant-matrix temporary bitcast are marked KnownNonNull, while addresses rebuilt from CreateThreadLocalAddress are explicitly marked NotKnownNonNull.
Changed symbols: Address; CodeGenFunction::CreateTempAllocaWithoutCast; CodeGenFunction::CreateTempAlloca; CodeGenFunction::CreateMemTemp; CodeGenFunction::EmitLoadOfScalar; CodeGenFunction::EmitStoreOfScalar; CodeGenFunction::EmitDeclRefLValue; CodeGenFunction::StartFunction
Behavioral change: Addresses created for allocas, function return storage, and the shown constant-matrix temporary bitcast now carry KnownNonNull.; Address::withPointer calls rebuilding an address from CreateThreadLocalAddress explicitly clear the property with NotKnownNonNull.; The change establishes a provenance invariant: non-null status is retained only where the shown construction is known to guarantee it, rather than being implicitly assumed after arbitrary pointer replacement.
Reproducer link: The issue involves a pointer loop; this commit changes Clang CodeGen tracking for pointer non-nullness.
Pass or subsystem link: Clang CodeGen; Address/LValue pointer-property propagation

Summary: This CodeGen change propagates an explicit known-non-null property through Address construction and pointer replacement. Stack allocas, return-value storage, and a constant-matrix temporary bitcast are marked KnownNonNull, while addresses rebuilt from CreateThreadLocalAddress are explicitly marked NotKnownNonNull.
Changed symbols: Address; CodeGenFunction::CreateTempAllocaWithoutCast; CodeGenFunction::CreateTempAlloca; CodeGenFunction::CreateMemTemp; CodeGenFunction::EmitLoadOfScalar; CodeGenFunction::EmitStoreOfScalar; CodeGenFunction::EmitDeclRefLValue; CodeGenFunction::StartFunction
Behavioral change: Addresses created for allocas, function return storage, and the shown constant-matrix temporary bitcast now carry KnownNonNull.; Address::withPointer calls rebuilding an address from CreateThreadLocalAddress explicitly clear the property with NotKnownNonNull.; The change establishes a provenance invariant: non-null status is retained only where the shown construction is known to guarantee it, rather than being implicitly assumed after arbitrary pointer replacement.
Reproducer link: The issue involves a pointer loop; this commit changes Clang CodeGen tracking for pointer non-nullness.
Pass or subsystem link: Clang CodeGen; Address/LValue pointer-property propagation
Causal explanation: This is a potentially relevant upstream CodeGen change because it can alter non-null information associated with pointers before LLVM optimization processes the generated IR, and the reproducer includes a pointer loop. However, the retrieved hunks contain no asm goto or asm-goto-output lowering, no ScalarEvolution or SCEVExpander change, and no evidence that this flag produces the loop-exit or sentinel condition implicated by isKnownSentinel and rewriteLoopExitValues. The connection is therefore indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.15
Build risk: The patch updates many Address construction and withPointer call sites, increasing the risk of inconsistent propagation of the new KnownNonNull/NotKnownNonNull invariant.; The retrieved selection contains no asm-goto CodeGen test or optimizer crash regression test.; A substantial number of hunks were omitted, so the definitions and downstream consumers of the new pointer-property flag are not available in the retrieved evidence.

top_candidates.subject: [NFC] Use single quotes for single char output during `printPipline`
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This is an NFC formatting change in pass-pipeline printing: single-character string literals are replaced with character literals when emitting punctuation in loop-pass-manager and SimplifyCFG pipeline descriptions.
Changed symbols: PassManager<Loop, LoopAnalysisManager, LoopStandardAnalysisResults &,...>::printPipeline; SimplifyCFGPass::printPipeline
Behavioral change: Pipeline-printing output continues to emit the same comma, angle-bracket, and semicolon characters; only the C++ literal form changes.; No CFG simplification, loop canonicalization, ScalarEvolution, or loop-exit-value transformation logic is changed.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM transform pass pipeline printing; SimplifyCFGPass
Causal explanation: Although the commit touches Scalar-transform directory files and SimplifyCFGPass has loop-related options in its surrounding context, the retrieved candidate hunks modify only raw_ostream punctuation emission in printPipeline methods. They do not alter the optimizer IR, asm-goto lowering, ScalarEvolution, SCEVExpander, isKnownSentinel, or rewriteLoopExitValues behavior implicated by the crash.
Causal confidence: 0.01
Build risk: NFC source-level literal substitution with no algorithmic or ABI change visible.; No candidate test additions or behavior-sensitive test updates were retrieved.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert restores ScalarEvolution handling for llvm.experimental.guard independently of AssumptionCache guard caching. It records whether a function contains guards, scans experimental_guard users for guards dominating a queried block or loop header, uses their conditions in guarded-entry and loop-guard reasoning, and permits selected zero-extension and signed-nowrap analyses to proceed when guards exist even if a maximum backedge count cannot be computed. evidence: Directly changes the reproducer's defining feature: asm goto outputs on indirect callbr edges.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: CodeGenFunction::EmitAsmStmt is changed to correctly materialize asm-goto output values on indirect callbr edges. For asm goto statements with outputs, the change splits every indirect destination into a synthetic block, records the callbr result or extracted aggregate elements per synthetic successor, redirects the callbr destinations, and emits the output stores in each corresponding successor block.
Changed symbols: CodeGenFunction::EmitAsmStmt; llvm::CallBrInst; CBRRegResults
Behavioral change: Retains the generated callbr instruction so its indirect destinations and returned output values can be processed after creation.; When an asm goto has register outputs, splits all callbr indirect destinations rather than leaving output handling only on the fallthrough path.; Creates per-successor output values from the callbr result, using the result directly for one output or extractvalue operations for multiple outputs.; Emits asm output stores in each synthetic indirect-destination block before its branch to the original destination, changing the CFG and SSA/value placement seen by later optimization passes.

index b9d67beda2f6..f3d263cbde2e 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopStrengthReduce.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopStrengthReduce.cpp
@@ -4984,0 +4985,23 @@ void LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceByDeletingCostlyFormulas() {
+// Check if Best and Reg are SCEVs separated by a constant amount C, and if so
+// would the addressing offset +C would be legal where the negative offset -C is
+// not.
+static bool IsSimplerBaseSCEVForTarget(const TargetTransformInfo &TTI,
+                                       ScalarEvolution &SE, const SCEV *Best,
+                                       const SCEV *Reg,
+                                       MemAccessTy AccessType) {
+  if (Best->getType() != Reg->getType())
+    return false;
+  const auto *Diff = dyn_cast<SCEVConstant>(SE.getMinusSCEV(Best, Reg));
+  if (!Diff)
+    return false;
+
+  return TTI.isLegalAddressingMode(
+             AccessType.MemTy, /*BaseGV=*/nullptr,
+             /*BaseOffset=*/Diff->getAPInt().getSExtValue(),
+             /*HasBaseReg=*/false, /*Scale=*/0, AccessType.AddrSpace) &&
+         !TTI.isLegalAddressingMode(
+             AccessType.MemTy, /*BaseGV=*/nullptr,
+             /*BaseOffset=*/-Diff->getAPInt().getSExtValue(),
+             /*HasBaseReg=*/false, /*Scale=*/0, AccessType.AddrSpace);
+}
+

diff --git a/flang/lib/Lower/ConvertArrayConstructor.cpp b/flang/lib/Lower/ConvertArrayConstructor.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..2343a8a2edc7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/flang/lib/Lower/ConvertArrayConstructor.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,538 @@
+//===- ConvertArrayConstructor.cpp -- Array Constructor ---------*- C++ -*-===//
+//
+// Part of the LLVM Project, under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.
+// See https://llvm.org/LICENSE.txt for license information.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#include "flang/Lower/ConvertArrayConstructor.h"
+#include "flang/Evaluate/expression.h"
+#include "flang/Lower/AbstractConverter.h"
+#include "flang/Lower/ConvertExprToHLFIR.h"
+#include "flang/Lower/ConvertType.h"
+#include "flang/Lower/StatementContext.h"
+#include "flang/Lower/SymbolMap.h"
+#include "flang/Optimizer/Builder/HLFIRTools.h"
+#include "flang/Optimizer/Builder/Todo.h"
+#include "flang/Optimizer/HLFIR/HLFIROps.h"
+
+// Array constructors are lowered with three different strategies.
+// All strategies are not possible with all array constructors.
+//
+// - Strategy 1: runtime approach (RuntimeTempStrategy).
+//   This strategy works will all array constructors, but will create more
+//   complex code that is harder to optimize. An allocatable temp is created,
+//   it may be unallocated if the array constructor length parameters or extent
+//   could not be computed. Then, the runtime is called to push lowered
+//   ac-value (array constructor elements) into the allocatable. The runtime
+//   will allocate or reallocate as needed while values are being pushed.
+//   In the end, the allocatable contain a temporary with all the array
+//   constructor evaluated elements.
+//

+//   This strategy can only be used if the array constructor extent and length

steps.subject: [Clang] refactor CodeGenFunction::EmitAsmStmt NFC

evidence: Refactors the exact Clang inline-asm output emission routine later used to implement indirect-edge outputs.
The patch is explicitly NFC and retains the prior output-store algorithm, so it is much weaker than the later semantic CFG change.
features: asm-output-stores, clang-codegen, inline-asm, nfc-refactor, path:clang/lib/CodeGen/CGStmt.cpp, path:llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Refactors CodeGenFunction::EmitAsmStmt by extracting asm-output conversion, validation, and store emission into the new helper EmitAsmStores. The existing two UpdateAsmCallInst call sites are adjusted to pass the result directly, and the former inlined output-store loop is replaced by a helper call; the commit subject explicitly labels the change NFC.
Changed symbols: CodeGenFunction::EmitAsmStmt; EmitAsmStores; UpdateAsmCallInst
Behavioral change: Moves the existing asm-output result processing and stores from EmitAsmStmt into EmitAsmStores without changing the visible conversion or store logic.; Removes explicit cast<llvm::CallBase>(*Result) at two UpdateAsmCallInst call sites and passes *Result directly.
Assertion or trace link: asm goto outputs; EmitAsmStmt
Reproducer link: The touched function emits inline-asm results and their output stores, a frontend area relevant to asm goto with outputs.
Pass or subsystem link: Clang CodeGen; inline-asm emission
Causal explanation: The commit touches the frontend routine that emits asm outputs, but its retrieved hunks preserve the former output-store algorithm in a helper and are described as NFC. There is no retrieved change to asm-goto indirect-edge semantics, CFG construction, ScalarEvolution, SCEVExpander, or loop-exit-value rewriting. The connection is therefore limited to shared codegen vicinity, not evidence of a changed condition that would produce the reported optimizer crash.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Refactors a large block of asm-output conversion and store-emission logic into a static helper.; The retrieved distance-0 hunks contain no regression test changes.; The subject's NFC designation is evidence against an intended semantic change, though refactoring can still expose integration mistakes.

Summary: This commit removes CallBrInst handling from InstCombine's constant-expression cast-call transformation and explicitly marks callbr unsupported in that path. In particular, it stops rebuilding a callbr with CreateCallBr and removes special PHI-placement handling for the callbr default destination, enforcing that transformConstExprCastCall is not entered for callbr.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::transformConstExprCastCall; InstCombinerImpl::visitCallBase
Behavioral change: InstCombine no longer transforms a CallBrInst through transformConstExprCastCall.; The transformation now asserts that its input is not a CallBrInst because callbr has no single post-definition insertion point suitable for the transformation.; InstCombine no longer recreates callbr instructions or treats their default destination as the special block for PHI handling in this transformation.
Assertion or trace link: CallBr's don't have a single point after a def to insert at
Reproducer link: The issue involves asm goto outputs, whose control-flow-sensitive IR handling is represented by CallBrInst.; The removed handling concerns callbr output values, indirect destinations, and PHI placement, all of which can affect CFG/value form seen by later optimization passes.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; CallBrInst; asm goto control-flow IR
Causal explanation: This is directly relevant to asm-goto/callbr IR and changes optimizer behavior around callbr-produced values and indirect control-flow edges. Such a change could alter the CFG or SSA form subsequently consumed by loop analyses and SCEV expansion. However, the retrieved hunks do not modify ScalarEvolution, SCEVExpander, rewriteLoopExitValues, or loop canonicalization, and they provide no direct evidence that this transformation reaches the reported isKnownSentinel crash.
Causal confidence: 0.42

@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+//===-- CallBrPrepare - Prepare callbr for code generation ----------------===//
+//
+// Part of the LLVM Project, under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.
+// See https://llvm.org/LICENSE.txt for license information.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+//
+// This pass lowers callbrs in LLVM IR in order to to assist SelectionDAG's
+// codegen.
+//
+// In particular, this pass assists in inserting register copies for the output
+// values of a callbr along the edges leading to the indirect target blocks.
+// Though the output SSA value is defined by the callbr instruction itself in
+// the IR representation, the value cannot be copied to the appropriate virtual
+// registers prior to jumping to an indirect label, since the jump occurs
+// within the user-provided assembly blob.
+//
+// Instead, those copies must occur separately at the beginning of each
+// indirect target. That requires that we create a separate SSA definition in
+// each of them (via llvm.callbr.landingpad), and may require splitting
+// critical edges so we have a location to place the intrinsic. Finally, we
+// remap users of the original callbr output SSA value to instead point to the
+// appropriate llvm.callbr.landingpad value.
+//
+// Ideally, this could be done inside SelectionDAG, or in the
+// MachineInstruction representation, without the use of an IR-level intrinsic.
+// But, within the current framework, it’s simpler to implement as an IR pass.
+// (If support for callbr in GlobalISel is implemented, it’s worth considering
+// whether this is still required.)
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/Passes.h"
+#include "llvm/IR/BasicBlock.h"
+#include "llvm/IR/Function.h"
+#include "llvm/IR/Instructions.h"
+#include "llvm/InitializePasses.h"
+#include "llvm/Pass.h"
+
+using namespace llvm;
+
+#define DEBUG_TYPE "callbrprepare"
+
+namespace {
+
+class CallBrPrepare : public FunctionPass {
+public:
+  CallBrPrepare() : FunctionPass(ID) {}
+  static char ID;
+  void getAnalysisUsage(AnalysisUsage &AU) const override;
+  bool runOnFunction(Function &Fn) override;
+};
+
+} // end anonymous namespace
+
+char CallBrPrepare::ID = 0;
+INITIALIZE_PASS(CallBrPrepare, DEBUG_TYPE, "Prepare callbr", false, false)
+
+FunctionPass *llvm::createCallBrPass() { return new CallBrPrepare(); }
+
+void CallBrPrepare::getAnalysisUsage(AnalysisUsage &AU) const {
+  AU.setPreservesAll();
+}
+
+bool CallBrPrepare::runOnFunction(Function &Fn) {
+  for (BasicBlock &BB : Fn) {
+    auto *CBR = dyn_cast<CallBrInst>(BB.getTerminator());
+    if (!CBR)
+      continue;
+    // TODO: something interesting.
+    // https://discourse.llvm.org/t/rfc-syncing-asm-goto-with-outputs-with-gcc/65453/8
+  }
+  return false;
+}
